tagline: Farm miles, a castle, and a hedge grown over the road.
intro: Pisgah Pike, KY 1967, starts just north of US 60 between Versailles and Lexington and runs north for five miles through Woodford County farm country to Old Frankfort Pike. Along the way it passes through the Pisgah Rural Historic District, 4,035 acres roughly bounded by South Elkhorn Creek, US 60 and Big Sink Road.
A colony from Virginia settled here in 1784 and named the place for Mount Pisgah, the mountain in the Hebrew Bible. The railroad came through in 1888, and the post office lasted from 1890 to 1931.

moments.title: The Kentucky Castle
moments.text: Rex and Caroline Martin began a castle here in 1969 after a trip to Germany, divorced in 1975 and left it unfinished, and for years it stood as a roadside oddity.

moments.title: Pisgah
moments.text: Pisgah Presbyterian Church was founded with the settlement in 1784 and has met in its present building since 1812.

moments.title: WinStar Farm
moments.text: Where the pike runs beside the old Silver Pool farm, an Osage orange hedge has grown so tall that it arches over the road, and the National Register counts it as historic.
